products.name: WhyLabs
products.note: Data-centric AI observability; statistical profiling; privacy-preserving monitoring

reading.body:
WhyLabs, an AI observability company focused on data-centric monitoring and privacy-preserving logging, has discontinued operations, though its open-source whylogs standard remains available.

The company occupied a niche in AI governance—the tools that let teams monitor whether AI systems are behaving as intended without exposing raw data. This work matters because observability is foundational to safe AI deployment. A system you cannot measure is a system you cannot control, and controlling AI requires understanding its inputs and outputs in production. WhyLabs positioned statistical profiling and privacy-preserving methods as the approach to this problem, meaning it tried to solve monitoring without creating new data security risks.

The closure leaves a gap in commercial tooling for this category, though the persistence of whylogs as open-source infrastructure suggests the underlying need remains. The data does not indicate why the company shut down, whether due to market demand, capital constraints, or competitive pressure. It also does not cover whether other vendors now serve the observability niche, or whether enterprises have moved this function in-house. For teams that adopted WhyLabs as a dependency, the closure forces a choice between maintaining whylogs independently or migrating to alternatives.
